newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican guerrillas claim members tortured.
newsitem.headline: Mexican guerrillas claim members tortured.

text.p: The clandestine Mexican guerrilla group the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) said on Sunday that one of its members was being held and tortured by the Mexican army.
The guerrilla leader known as Commandante Insurgente Hermenegildo said in a statement that a member of the group, Benito Bahena Maldonado, was being held in military prisons.
"Benito Bahena Maldonado is a prisoner of war, a fighter for the insurgent army, who finds himself in the hands of the Mexican federal army," the EPR said in the statement.
"We can confirm that he is being savagely tortured...," the EPR said.
A spokesman for the Ministry of Defence said he was not aware of the statement and could not make an immediate comment.

The EPR burst on the scene in Mexico in June 1996, calling for the overthrow of the government of President Ernesto Zedillo. After a series of bloody clashes with Mexican authorities in several states, the Marxist guerrillas turned instead turned to a propaganda war.
The violence returned, however, when the heavily-armed EPR and the military clashed in the state of Guerrero in May in battles that left several dead.
Many leftist politicians have claimed the army has used the guerrilla activity as an excuse to crack down on peasant organisers in the poorest of the Mexican states.

The EPR said in its latest statement that Bahena Maldonado was kidnapped, along with a supporter of the guerrillas, in a park in the port city of Acapulco on June 24. It said both people were members of a well-known local peasant rights activist group.
The guerrillas said the EPR supporter, Domingo Ayala, was later released after having been tortured.
